findings.title: Bound serialized sub-object counts before allocating nodes
findings.reason: The scene header supplies node_budget and sub_objects accepts a file count n against only that budget, then resizes the Node vector before verifying that the remaining bytes can hold those records. A tiny truncated binary/named scene can declare both counts INT_MAX and trigger allocation of about112GB (52 bytes per Node), allocator abort or process exhaustion instead of a bounded ModelError. The512MiB per-file limit does not constrain this allocation.
findings.bounded_correction: Before resize, check cumulative arithmetic/representable node lengths and a conservative format/version-correct minimum serialized record bound against remaining bytes; use an explicit resource ceiling or bounded/checked reservation as needed. Preserve valid node order/layout and add a tiny exaggerated-count file control that refuses without a large allocation.
findings.evidence: Static source defect; no deliberately excessive allocation was executed by this reviewer.

findings.title: Propagate override-directory and entry read errors
findings.reason: sorted_entries converts read_dir errors to an empty list and flattens individual entry errors. find_dir likewise resolves an inaccessible/existing directory as absent. A failed OBJECTS or named-scene directory enumeration can therefore silently omit physical overrides and produce a successful partial/table-only store, contradicting file-specific refusal/no fallback behavior.
findings.bounded_correction: Distinguish genuinely absent optional directories from enumeration/type/entry failures; propagate failures as ModelError with the affected path. Preserve successful enumeration order and valid no-OBJECTS installations. Add bounded I/O-error controls through actual resolver/enumerator code (injectable filesystem boundary is acceptable when permissions cannot be reproduced portably).
findings.evidence: Static error handling; no permissions/assets were changed or native run performed.

findings.title: Refuse incomplete or failed original reports before declaring comparison success
findings.reason: compare_original parses recognized rows independently but ignores original done/check results, catalogue cardinality/uniqueness and geometry terminal/depth/group completeness; its only completeness guard is at least one input row. The Lua driver only rejects zero compared counters. A truncated original ending after one matching model-scene, a repeated matching scene, or an otherwise matching report whose original done says failures>0 can consequently yield zero mismatches and done failures0. Existing synthetic comparator fixtures intentionally omit the real report envelope, so they do not expose this false green.
findings.bounded_correction: Validate the supported original report contract/completion before comparison, including declared catalogue identity/cardinality and geometry depth/terminal/call correspondence. Preserve legitimate catalogue-off, explicit refused/capped/unbacked modes and original partial-write observations; do not require unsupported physical successes. Replace partial positive collaborators with coherent report envelopes and add truncate/duplicate/missing-terminal/failed-done controls through the real comparator.
findings.reuse_limit: The actual three complete hash-pinned originals were independently inspected and their metadata/215 calls compared below; this reusable-checker defect does not invalidate those concrete matched measurements.

findings.title: Check scene bounds before narrowing i64 to usize
findings.reason: check_scene converts a positive i64 scene to usize before comparing with scene count. On32-bit targets,4294967297 wraps to1 and passes, so public scene/triangle can answer the wrong model rather than refuse. The Lua whole-number range currently permits that input.
findings.bounded_correction: Compare the original i64 with actual scene-count/target representability bounds before conversion, then convert. Add a positive wide-ID control that exercises the32-bit boundary or a checked conversion helper with an explicit target ceiling. Leave valid IDs and numerical behavior unchanged.
findings.evidence: Target-width source defect, not an observed failure of the current Windows x64 retail runs.
